argv:
Rewrite the text following the rules of The Elements of Style.

Omit needless words. Every word must tell. Use the active voice. Put
statements in positive form: say what something is, not what it is not.

Use definite, specific, concrete language in preference to the vague and
abstract. Keep related words together. Express coordinate ideas in parallel
form. Place the emphatic words of a sentence at the end.

Make the paragraph the unit of composition, each with a clear topic sentence.
Write with nouns and verbs rather than adjectives and adverbs. Avoid
qualifiers such as "rather", "very", and "little".

request.user_prompt:
Rewrite the passage below according to your style instructions.

Output only the rewritten passage. Do not add a preamble, a title, an
explanation, or any commentary about the changes you made.

<passage>
Operators must ensure the guard is lowered to within the recommended clearance of the workpiece before the blade is engaged, although the tensioning wheel should be checked periodically throughout a shift regardless of guard position, since drift in tension can occur even when the machine has not been used continuously. The lower blade guide must be inspected for wear whenever the blade has been changed, unless the replacement blade is of the same width and pitch as the one it replaces, in which case a visual check may be sufficient provided the operator has completed the tensioning procedure described elsewhere in this manual. Loose clothing and jewelry should not be worn near the machine, and long hair must be tied back. Operators may leave the work area only after the blade has come to a complete stop, though the machine's residual heat can persist for several minutes and caution is advised.
</passage>

response.text:
Before engaging the blade, lower the guard to the recommended clearance above the workpiece. Check the tensioning wheel periodically throughout the shift regardless of guard position; tension can drift even when the machine sits idle.

Inspect the lower blade guide for wear whenever you change the blade. If the replacement blade matches the original in width and pitch, a visual check suffices—but only after you complete the tensioning procedure described elsewhere in this manual.

Remove loose clothing and jewelry before operating the machine. Tie back long hair.

Wait until the blade stops completely before leaving the work area. The machine retains heat for several minutes afterward, so use caution.
